title: Trump's Big Choice: Deal or 'Annihilate' Iran?
summary:
Imagine standing at a giant podium in New York City, in front of leaders from almost every country in the world. That's the United Nations General Assembly. On Tuesday, President Donald Trump gave a speech there with a huge question: should the US make a peace deal with Iran, or 'annihilate' it?

Trump said he faces a 'big decision.' He also said a deal might happen right after the US elections in November. During his speech, only one person from Iran's team watched.

But here's the surprising part: on the very same day, US and Iranian officials actually talked! They didn't meet face to face. A mediator from Qatar carried messages back and forth between them. Iran's Foreign Minister, Abbas Araghchi, met with US envoy Steve Witkoff. Iran said it wants the fighting to stop everywhere and no more 'acts of aggression' from the US.

Trump also talked about trying to end the war between Russia and Ukraine. He said, 'We will get that one done.' He even signed a deal with Denmark about Greenland.

So what happens next? Will there be a deal, or more fighting? Even Trump says he's not sure yet. The whole world is watching.
why_it_matters: When two powerful countries can fight or talk, it changes prices, safety, and whether families far away live in fear — so even kids hear about it in the news.

background_read: The United Nations (a group where almost every country in the world meets to talk about big problems) holds a huge meeting every September in New York, and leaders from all over give speeches there.
Iran (a large country in the Middle East) and the United States have been unfriendly to each other for many years, and the two governments almost never talk directly.
Qatar (a small, very rich country on the Arabian Gulf) often acts as a messenger between countries that refuse to sit down together, which is why it helped pass messages this time.
Article_Structure: WHO: President Donald Trump, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, US envoy Steve Witkoff, and a mediator from Qatar.
WHAT: Trump told the United Nations he faces a 'big decision' on Iran — a peace deal or 'annihilate' it — while on the same day US and Iranian officials traded messages through Qatar.
WHERE: At the United Nations General Assembly in New York City, with talks carried out indirectly rather than face to face.
WHY: Because the world is waiting to see whether the US and Iran move toward a peace deal after the November elections or toward more fighting.

perspectives.description: They say that even indirect talks through a messenger like Qatar are better than fighting, because a deal could stop a war before it grows bigger.
They worry that making a deal would only give Iran more time and money, and that nice words cannot be trusted.

perspectives.perspective: People who say it's too early to tell
perspectives.description: They point out that Trump himself says he is not sure yet, so nobody knows if this ends in a deal or in more fighting.
